extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, proofreaders, and publishers preparing and managing manuscripts and publications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, editing, and publishing manuscripts across print and electronic formats, covering punctuation, citations, typography, tables, headings, and rights. Intended to be used by editorial staff and authors to ensure consistent house style and correct publication mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series of works / series titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines on treatment of series and series titles—including ISBN/ISSN, capitalization (capitalized but not italicized), placement (covers, front matter), proofing, and source citations for series and multivolume works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include ISBN and ISSN for series (1.32); series titles capitalized but not italicized in book review/notes (1.98; 8.2, 8.176); place on covers/jackets and in front matter (1.70; 1.4, 1.18); proofread (2.108); provide source-citation guidance for series and multivolume works (14.86; 14.123-26; see also multivolume works, volumes and volume numbers). Note unfinished date ranges, working papers in series, and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serial publications and serial rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on serial publications and related copyright/registration and rights issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to copyright registration forms for serial publications (4.48) and serial rights (first or second rights) (4.64); see also guidance under periodicals. Consult sections on distribution, subsidiary rights, and permissions for serials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commas and punctuation in series
rubrics_metrics.description: How to punctuate series/series of elements within a sentence and related punctuation interactions (ampersands, colons, em dashes, semicolons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed cross-references: series and ampersands (6.21); colons to introduce series (6.61, 6.67); commas within series (6.19–21, 6.23); commas with em dashes (6.86); semicolons within series (6.60, 6.129). Follow specific section rules for complex interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened citations (criteria and use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and criteria for using shortened citations in notes and text versus abbreviated titles; when shortened forms are appropriate and how to cross-reference to full citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See rules and examples for shortened citations (14.29–36) and distinctions vs. abbreviated titles (14.59). Includes guidance for anonymous works in text citations (15.34), cross-references to the full citation (14.31), discouraged forms (idem, op. cit., loc. cit.) (14.35–36), and examples/variations (14.23). Also guidance on same-author same-year shortened forms (15.29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source citations (overall principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose, basic elements, and systems for source citations; use of citation-management software; house style and flexibility versus consistency; hyperlinking and electronic considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose and basic elements (14.1; 14.100); basic systems and differences (1.108; 13.64; 14.2–3); citation management software recommendations (14.5, 14.12); editing and author queries about source citations (2.62–64); house style, flexibility, and need for consistency (2.64; 14.4); hyperlinks and electronic citation practices; remedies for excessive annotation (abbreviations, combining notes, avoiding overlong notes 14.56–60). See also author-date and notes/bibliography systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source citations for specific media and contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for citing various types of sources (e.g., journal articles, blog posts, classical works, databases, newspapers, legal style, manuscripts, multiauthor volumes, blogs, chapters, poems, songs, sound recordings, supplementary data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides section-level rules and examples for many source types: journal articles (14.23, 14.33, 14.171), blog posts and comments (14.208), classical Greek and Latin works (14.244), databases (14.276), newspaper articles (14.196), legal style (14.275–279), manuscript collections (14.229), multiauthor volumes and chapters (14.32, 14.108), poetry extracts and quotations (13.72; 13.66–67), songs and sound recordings (8.194; 14.263–64), supplementary data (14.112; 14.187), and many more. Follow the specific section cited for formatting and element order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source-citation mechanics: shortened forms, DOIs, URLs
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when and how to use shortened citations, short forms for DOIs and URLs, and handling very long titles in citation entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortened citations: see criteria (14.29) and examples/variations (14.23); short forms for DOIs and URLs (14.10); treatment of very long titles in reference-list entries (14.97); cross-references to full citations (14.31); avoid discouraged classical citation forms (idem, op. cit.) (14.35–36). Guidance also touches on table source notes (3.77) and text citation placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source notes and their use
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use source notes and how they relate to tables, previously published materials, and attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source notes referenced for previously published materials (1.50; 2.46; 4.78; 14.54) and for tables (2.31; 2.61; 3.76–77; 3.81). See also attribution, illustration credits, and relation to notes and bibliographies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous print/electronic publishing considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific concerns and practices when publishing simultaneously in print and electronic formats (format differences, markup, illustrations, ISSNs, page ranges, proofreading, version control, source citation considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes on common use (1.2), relationships to formal markup languages (1.117), format differences (1.77), handling illustrations (1.107; 3.10; 3.17; 3.26), ISSN considerations (1.79, 1.86), letters to the editor (1.101), noting differences between versions (1.78; 1.81; 1.87; 14.16), page ranges (1.81), proofreading (2.140), version control (1.112), tables (1.106) and source-citation considerations (14.16). See also multiple formats and electronic supplementary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary data and supplementary materials (electronic)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle supplementary electronic data and materials for books and journals: linking, notation, citation, and notation in tables of contents and print versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic supplementary data for books and journals: designate and hyperlink (1.96; 1.78; 14.112; 14.187); note in print versions (1.78); illustrate placement in the table of contents (1.78; 1.87). Proofread and provide source citations for supplementary materials (14.112; 14.187).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spaces and spacing (types and uses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing the use and marking of different space widths (em, en, hair, thin, thick), their use with punctuation and in specific contexts (math expressions, units, typography), and proofreading/marking guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Em spaces (2.126; 3.23; 3.54; 6.120); en spaces (6.120; 13.29); hair spaces (6.5; 6.11; 6.120); thin spaces (definition p.988; use in French materials and math 11.28–32; 12.17, 12.42); spacing with units of measurement (6.119; 6.121; 7.44; 9.16); spaces between sentences (2.9; 2.80); spacing in table titles (3.54); justification, nonbreaking spaces, and marking/manuscript/proof techniques (2.125; 2.98; 2.131). See also leading and line spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special characters and character handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on special characters: listing, markup, conversion errors, fonts, Unicode, and how to prepare/manuscript special characters for production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author’s list of special characters recommended (2.3; 2.16; 11.21; 11.122; 12.13); conversion errors common in special characters (2.80; 2.137); described in angle brackets (2.16); bitmapped images for special characters (2.137); generic markup of special characters (2.81); resources and tables for special characters (tables 11.1–5); Unicode and language-specific resources (11.2; 11.70–75). Pay attention to language-specific tables and specialized fonts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software and electronic-tool issues in publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: How software affects manuscript conversion, special characters, sorting, indexing, and other editorial tasks; recommended types of tools and concerns about conversion errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to types of software (artwork, citation management, document comparison, indexing, manuscript editing, manuscript preparation, mathematical copy, page layout, PDF proofreading tools) and common conversion errors (2.80; 2.113; 2.137). Sorting functions and computer-sorting interactions (14.65, 14.67; 15.17) and issues with special characters and Unicode. Use appropriate tools and test electronic formats (1.92; 2.138–39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling and orthography
rubrics_metrics.description: House-style expectations for spelling (US vs British), discipline-specific spelling, checking, consistency, common errors, and handling spelled-out abbreviations/numbers and transliteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: British-style and non-US spellings (7.3); discipline-specific spellings (7.2); checking and consistency (2.89; 2.65); common errors and author queries (2.69; 2.111); editors’ notes (1.45); style sheets recommended for spelling management (2.55); handling orthographic reforms and transliteration (11.38; 11.43; 11.45).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidiary rights and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of subsidiary rights, economic considerations, author’s retention, electronic rights, translation and non-US publication distribution, moral rights, university licenses, and public-access policy interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsidiary-rights categories and distinctions from basic rights (4.64; 4.17); author’s electronic use and retention (4.66; 4.18); distribution outside the US and non-US publication issues (4.34; 4.29–30); economic considerations and granting permissions (4.65–71); translation (4.34; 4.64), moral rights (4.15), university licenses (4.67), and public-access policies (4.68). See also copyright and permissions sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive editing vs mechanical editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between substantive editing (content-level changes) and mechanical or copyediting, including when each is applied in the editorial process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive editing referenced (2.48; 2.50; 2.51) and mechanical editing tasks identified elsewhere (1.116). Use style sheets and manuscript-preparation guidelines to coordinate substantive and mechanical changes; mark permissible changes in proofs (13.7; 13.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Superscripts and subscripts usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of superscripts and subscripts in classical works, chemical notation, mathematics, music, and notes—covering alignment, spacing, marking, and when to use italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined and marking manuscript guidance (2.94; p.988). In mathematical expressions (12.36–38; 12.63; 12.67), alignment and spacing (12.16–17; 12.38), and chemical notation (8.149). Superscripts used for powers of ten, note reference numbers (14.19; 14.24), and in table notes (3.79). Subscripts used in chemical symbols and mathematical notation; provide marking and typesetting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: structure, formatting, and editorial rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules for tables: structure, column and stub heads, alignment, formatting of numbers and words, notes, numbering, placement, attribution, permissions, accessibility, shading, runovers, totals, statistical significance, units, and machine-readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic structure and figure examples (3.52; fig. 3.11); column heads (format, alignment) (3.71; 3.53; 3.56); body and cells alignment and formatting (3.70–74); stub columns and runover lines (3.59–64; 3.61); numbering and numbering conventions (1.57; 2.29; 3.50; 3.54; 16.116); notes to tables (3.76–80) including source notes (3.77) and significance levels (3.80; fig. 3.22); placement and pagination interactions (3.51; 1.8); electronic files and machine-readable tables (2.26; 3.47; 1.106); accessibility issues (3.88); permissions and fair use (3.77; 4.91); shading (3.64); resources and rules summarized in figs and sections (3.47–88). Use consistent formatting and cross-checking with text citations (2.32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular material and tabs
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on tabular material handling in manuscripts and electronic formats, including HTML tables, manuscript-preparation guidelines, and proofreading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabs and tabular materials in manuscripts: use of tabs (2.11; 2.12; 2.19; 2.21; 2.24; 2.80); manuscript-preparation guidance for tabular material (2.29); HTML-format tables (1.118); placement, proofing, and submission procedures. See also tables: structure and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style sheets (editorial) and their use
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and use of editorial style sheets (paper and electronic) for manuscript editing; proofreader’s use and how they aid consistency and manuscript preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style sheets defined (p.988); use in manuscript editing and proofreader’s practice (2.55; 2.83; 2.111–12); electronic style sheets referenced (pp. 988, 990). Create and maintain style sheets for house style, queries, and proof corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheads and running heads
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for subheads: definition, levels, capitalization, punctuation, placement, use as alternatives to page numbers in source citations, and interaction with running heads and tables of contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined and cross-referenced (p.988). Levels, placement, and typographic style (1.56; 2.59); capitalization and punctuation rules (1.56; 6.14); use as alternatives to page numbers in citations (14.160, 14.174); editing and proofreading practices (2.59; 2.113; 2.134); usage in tables and running heads (3.86; 1.12; 2.76). Sideheads and spanner/decked heads discussed (3.53; 3.57).

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntax, sentence structure, and grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on sentence-level grammar and syntax: sentence types, clause structure, SVO pattern, subject-verb agreement, subjunctive mood, expletives, negation, parallel structure, and bias-free language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax overview and rules (5.210–48): defined and explained with cross-references for avoiding gender bias (5.255), parallel structure (5.242–45), negation (5.230–38), subject-verb agreement (5.138–143; 5.205), sentence types and traditional sentence structures (5.211–20), clauses and subordination (5.225–28), and cleft sentences (5.246–48). See also punctuation interactions and quotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text citations (in-text citation practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and formats for text citations: basic approach, placement in text, page/volume locators, punctuation conventions, treatment of multiple and repeated references, and relation to reference lists and notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic approach and format with examples/variations (15.5; 15.9; fig. 15.2); placement in text (15.25–28); page, volume numbers, and locators (15.8; 15.23); punctuation rules (brackets, commas, semicolons) (15.7; 15.9; 15.22; 15.24; 15.28); shortened citations in text (13.66–70; 15.29; 15.34); cross-checking and multiple references (2.32; 15.30); biblical and classical citations (14.239; 14.242). Ensure consistency with surrounding syntax (15.28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of works (capitalization, formatting, and indexing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive rules on rendering titles of works: capitalization (headline vs sentence style), italics, handling subtitles, series and volume notation, non-English works, placement on covers/jackets, indexing and alphabetizing, and treatment in source citations and running text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalization and style choices: headline-style vs sentence-style capitalization (8.157–62; 8.158); subtitle rules (8.158; 8.164–65; 14.87–91), punctuation with colons/semicolons when connecting titles and subtitles (1.19; 8.164–67; 14.89–91); series, volumes, edition notation (8.176; 8.175; 14.113); handling double titles and connecting words (8.167; 14.91); titles on covers/jackets and front matter (1.69; 1.70; 1.4); capitalization rules for non-English works and translations (11.6–10; 11.27; 11.89); indexing and alphabetizing titles, including articles and disregarded leading articles (16.48–56; 14.98); italicized terms within titles (8.173); special categories (artworks, exhibitions, musical works, blogs) have particular rules (8.57; 8.194; 8.192; 14.206). Cross-check titles in proofs (2.32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page elements and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: What to include on a title page (author names, foreword authors, edition number, publication/distribution information, place/date of publication), editing and proofreading guidance, and submission practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title page components and placement across pages (1.17–19); author/editor/translator names and crediting (1.19; 14.73; 14.82; 15.12); distribution and publication data to include (14.129; 14.141–142); edition number and new preface notes (1.26; 14.113); proofing and editing of the title page (2.57; 2.134); running heads omitted from title pages (1.11); submission instructions (2.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time designations and chronology formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format time-related information: a.m./p.m. abbreviations, chronology systems, days/months/eras, time zones, periods (centuries, decades), and hyphenation and capitalization conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations and numeric forms (a.m./p.m., 9.37–38; 10.41); chronology systems and eras (9.34; 9.64; 10.38); hyphenation rules referenced (7.89 sec. 1); time-of-day conventions (noon/midnight, 9.38; 24-hour system, 9.39–40); time zones and timestamps for electronic content (8.90; 14.191; 14.207; 14.209). Provide consistent styling for periods and inclusive years (9.64).
